function_v0.doc: SEP-0041 balance read \xe2\x80\x94 returns the REAL stored balance while the entry\nis alive, and 0 the moment it is evicted. No event marks the transition.
function_v0.name: balance

function_v0.doc:
Credit `to` with a REAL balance and emit a REAL transfer event, with an
attacker-chosen fuse.

`ttl_ledgers` is the number of ledgers the balance survives. Stellar
closes a ledger roughly every 5 seconds, so:
17280  ~= 1 day      (a plausible settlement window; sweep succeeds)
120960 ~= 7 days
60     ~= 5 minutes  (fast demo on testnet)

Nothing else about this function is hostile. It mints, it writes, it
emits. An auditor reading it sees a normal token.
function_v0.name: deposit

function_v0.doc:
Standard SEP-0041 transfer. Completely honest and symmetric \xe2\x80\x94 there is
no pause, no lock, no allow-list. It works perfectly for as long as the
balance entry is alive, which is exactly what makes a deposit-time test
sweep pass.

After eviction `read_balance` returns 0 (the entry no longer exists) and
this panics with "insufficient balance" \xe2\x80\x94 indistinguishable from the
exchange having already spent the funds.
function_v0.name: transfer
